audit.why: Yone taking most stages fits a 47.72% Sejuani win rate over 241 games — the one matchup in this slice she genuinely loses. Mortal Steel is 4s against Winter's Wrath's 9s and Arctic Assault's 18s, so he refreshes his trade pattern roughly twice for every one of hers, and Spirit Cleave shields him every 14s on top. The shape of the chart is right; the reasons given for it are what were wrong.

audit.whatIsWrong: The mid paragraph gives Soul Unbound's cooldown as 'roughly 22 seconds early' and never says it falls to 10, and Fate Sealed is never mentioned or timed anywhere in either layer.
audit.why: 22 seconds is only rank 1. By rank 5 Soul Unbound is 10 seconds — less than a Winter's Wrath rotation at rank 1 — so a plan built on 'track his E cooldown, it is roughly 22 seconds' silently stops working around level 9 and the player never learns why. Fate Sealed is 120/100/80 and pulls everyone it hits toward him, which is the ability that decides whether Sejuani's own engage or his lands first in the teamfights the entry says she should be playing for.
audit.corrected: Soul Unbound: 22/19/16/13/10s. Fate Sealed: 120/100/80s, blinks behind the last champion in a line and pulls everyone hit toward him.
sources: champ-data/_kits/yone.json (Soul Unbound 22/19/16/13/10; Fate Sealed 120/100/80, 'pulls all enemies hit towards him')

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer describes Soul Unbound as an escape four times: 'E cancels your Q knock-up and resets him out of danger instantly', 'E spirit-rewind lets him dodge your Q initiation entirely', 'makes him untouchable', 'lets him escape or dodge every subsequent Q engage attempt'. Soul Unbound is not an escape.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Yone's spirit leaves his body behind, gaining Move Speed. When this ability ends, Yone's spirit is forced back to his body.' The body stays where it was and he is dragged back to it — the ability tells you exactly where he will be and when. That is the single best piece of information Sejuani gets in this matchup and the content layer inverts it into a reason not to engage. The full layer already has it right in breakdown.cooldowns ('punish the body he snaps back to'), so the two layers of the same page currently contradict each other on the matchup's defining ability.
audit.corrected: Soul Unbound leaves his body behind and forces him back to it. Stand on the body, hold Frost stacks, and Permafrost him the instant he snaps home — he does not get to choose where he lands.
sources: champ-data/_kits/yone.json (Soul Unbound: 'Yone's spirit leaves his body behind ... When this ability ends, Yone's spirit is forced back to his body')
champ-data/sejuani.full.js (breakdown.cooldowns for this entry, which states it correctly)

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer says his 'soul-split passive means he heals part of that back' and that 'soul-split heals him through short trades'. Way of the Hunter does not heal. It deals magic damage on every second attack and raises his critical strike chance. Separately, Spirit Cleave's shield is never mentioned.
audit.why: A fabricated heal and a real shield, in opposite directions, both push the player toward the same wrong conclusion about who wins a short trade. The healing does not exist, so short trades are less lost than the entry claims; the shield does exist on a 14-second cooldown that scales with his attack speed, so it is the thing that actually absorbs the first Winter's Wrath arc. Naming the right mechanic changes the answer from 'never trade' to 'trade after the shield is spent'.
audit.corrected: Way of the Hunter is bonus magic damage every second attack plus crit chance — no healing. The absorption you feel is Spirit Cleave's shield, 14s and shortening with his attack speed.
sources: champ-data/_kits/yone.json (Way of the Hunter: 'deals magic damage with every second Attack ... critical strike chance is increased' — no heal flag; Spirit Cleave cd 14, shield flag, 'cooldown and cast time scale with attack speed')

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer refers to 'Permafrost armor', 'your Permafrost armor window' and 'the resistances your Permafrost passive and tank items provide'. Permafrost is Sejuani's E stun and has no passive or armour component.
audit.why: The resistances come from Frost Armor on Fury of the North, gained only after being out of combat and lost shortly after she takes damage. Against Yone the condition is the whole point — Mortal Steel pokes every 4 seconds, so any chip keeps Frost Armor down, and the player needs to know the buff is conditional to understand why he never seems to have it in this lane.
audit.corrected: Frost Armor comes from Fury of the North, out of combat only, and his 4-second Mortal Steel chip is exactly what keeps it off you.
sources: champ-data/_kits/sejuani.json (Fury of the North; Permafrost descriptions)

notes: Best find: the content layer calls Soul Unbound an escape four separate times — 'resets him out of danger instantly', 'dodge your Q initiation entirely', 'makes him untouchable', 'lets him escape or dodge every subsequent Q engage'. It is the opposite. Riot's text says his spirit leaves the body behind and is forced back to it when the ability ends, so the ability publishes exactly where he will be and when. That is the best information Sejuani gets in this lane and the entry converts it into the reason not to engage. Note that the FULL layer already states this correctly in breakdown.cooldowns ('punish the body he snaps back to') — the two layers of the same page currently contradict each other on the matchup's defining ability, and the content layer is the wrong one. Second: 'his soul-split passive means he heals part of that back' and 'soul-split heals him through short trades' are fabricated. Way of the Hunter deals magic damage every second attack and raises crit chance; there is no heal anywhere in Yone's kit. What is really absorbing the poke is Spirit Cleave's shield, on 14 seconds and shortening with his attack speed, which neither layer mentions. Third: the mid paragraph gives Soul Unbound as 'roughly 22 seconds early' and never says it reaches 10 by rank 5, so the tracking plan quietly expires around level 9.
